newsitem.title: ITALY: Troops in Albania force - who and how many.
newsitem.headline: Troops in Albania force - who and how many.

text.p: The Italian-led security force being assembled for deployment in Albania is expected to number up to 6,000 men.

Defence sources say it is likely to be led on the ground by General Luciano Forlani, the 57-year-old commander of Italy's Third Armoured Corps and a former commander of the Italian division assigned to NATO's rapid intervention forces.
Following are details of nations and numbers:
-- ITALY is expected to provide 2,000 to 2,500 troops, including mechanised infantry, paratroopers, light armoured forces, army and navy commando units and air support.

-- FRANCE, 1,000 troops made up of mechanised marine units plus helicopters, armoured personnel carriers and other armoured fighting vehicles including wheeled tanks. The French say they want to cover the port of Durres and the movement of supplies from there to the capital Tirana.
-- GREECE, 700 troops. Athens says it prefers to deploy its forces away from the south, where there is a large ethnic Greek minority.
-- SPAIN, 300 troops including a light infantry unit, a logistics unit, engineers and medics. Expected to be deployed near Durres.

AUSTRIA says it is prepared to contribute soldiers and police but will await the exact plan of operation from Italy before making any formal decision. DENMARK says it is considering possible participation.
The force will be deployed at Tirana airport and the Adriatic ports of Durres, Vlore and possibly Sarande to protect relief convoys around the country.
